fleet.name: factory
fleet.title: The Factory
fleet.description: An agent-native software-delivery control plane: PFactory prepares a governed plan, AIFactory builds it, TFactory verifies it, CFactory threads the whole run on one correlation key. This aggregate is the single entry point for an agent that wants to know what the fleet can do.

service.name: pfactory
service.title: PFactory
service.description: Governed planning grounded in live cloud/Backstage context. A planning session is ingested from an idea or spec, enriched with org/cloud context, decomposed, and scored by four review gates (architecture, security, best-practices, feasibility) that each return 0-1 with citations. A human approves, then PFactory emits governed GitHub issues and sets the RFC-0001 correlation key.

skills.name: plan-create
skills.description: Start a governed planning session from an idea or a spec. Give it a title, a description and the target repo; it returns a session id you use for every later step. This is the front of the PARR funnel: nothing reaches AIFactory without a plan.

skills.name: plan-enrich
skills.description: Pull live cloud and Backstage context into an existing planning session, so the plan is grounded in the org's real infrastructure and catalog rather than in guesses.

skills.name: plan-review
skills.description: Run the four review gates over a session: architecture, security, best-practices and feasibility. Each returns a 0-1 score with the citations behind it, so a low score can be argued with rather than merely obeyed.

skills.name: plan-approve
skills.description: Record the human governance decision on a reviewed session (approve or reject, with an optional note). PFactory will not emit work without it.

skills.name: plan-emit
skills.description: Emit the approved plan as governed GitHub issues and set the RFC-0001 correlation key that threads the work across AIFactory, TFactory and CFactory. Use this when a plan is signed off and ready to build.

skills.name: cloud-discover
skills.description: Run a read-only cloud posture assessment of an AWS, Azure or GCP account: enumerate resources, detect misconfigurations with Prowler (CIS/OCSF), build a service-topology diagram, and emit an accept/flag/reject verdict into findings/. Nothing is mutated.

service.name: aifactory
service.title: AIFactory
service.description: Spec-first build core. A task is created from a governed GitHub issue or a signed RFC-0002 task contract, then a planner -> coder (isolated git worktree) -> QA pipeline runs against a multi-provider model factory (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, vLLM, Codex, Copilot CLI). It can delegate the build to another coding agent, and it applies TFactory handbacks through its QA fixer.

skills.name: handover
skills.description: Hand the task you have been discussing interactively off to AIFactory's autonomous pipeline, so planner -> coder -> QA -> human-review runs in the background while you work on something else. Use it for anything you would otherwise babysit.

skills.name: aifactory-spec
skills.description: Kick off AIFactory spec creation for a new feature, driving the spec runner that turns a described feature into the spec the build pipeline consumes.

skills.name: task-create
skills.description: Start a build from a governed issue or a spec. Returns a task id and the RFC-0001 correlation key that threads this unit of work across the fleet.

skills.name: task-from-plan
skills.description: Build directly from a signed RFC-0002 task contract, skipping AIFactory's own planning stage. This is the trusted-plan fast path: PFactory has already decided WHAT and HOW, so the coder starts immediately.

skills.name: task-qa-fix
skills.description: Apply a TFactory handback: given the failing tests and the triage report, AIFactory's QA fixer writes the correction on the original task rather than starting a new build. This is the return leg of the AIFactory <-> TFactory loop.

skills.name: task-worktree
skills.description: Inspect the isolated git worktree a build is running in: its branch, path and whether the tree is clean. Use it to see what the coder has actually written before a PR exists.

skills.name: task-delegate
skills.description: Delegate a build to a different coding agent or executor instead of AIFactory's own coder, keeping the same task id and correlation key.

skills.name: providers-list
skills.description: List the model providers this AIFactory instance has configured, with model and transport for each. Read-only, and the cheapest way for an agent to learn what it can route to.

service.name: tfactory
service.title: TFactory
service.description: Autonomous test generation and execution. From a branch or PR plus acceptance criteria it runs planner -> gen-functional -> executor (sandboxed) -> evaluator -> triager across five lanes (unit, browser, api, integration, mutation). The evaluator grades every generated test on a 5-signal verdict - coverage delta, stability across re-runs, mutation score, flake lint and semantic relevance - so a pass means meaningful tests, not a green bar.

skills.name: tfactory
skills.description: Onboarding skill: how to work inside the TFactory codebase itself - the 4-agent pipeline, the LLM-provider abstraction (never call a vendor SDK directly), the workspace layout, the branching model, how to run the suite, and the non-negotiable conventions. Install this before changing TFactory, not before using it.

skills.name: handover-to-tfactory
skills.description: Hand a finished feature off to TFactory for polyglot test generation - from AIFactory, from Claude Code, or from any tool via the MCP control plane or a markdown/Gherkin/EARS acceptance-criteria file. Drives the full pipeline across the five lanes and produces a triage report, optionally committing the tests to the feature branch and commenting on the PR.

skills.name: tfactory-watch
skills.description: Poll a running TFactory task to completion, then pick up its triage report and check the generated tests actually cover the acceptance criteria. One check per invocation - drive it under /loop for a hands-off round trip.

skills.name: tfactory-fixloop
skills.description: Close the AIFactory <-> TFactory loop hands-off: hand the correction back to AIFactory, wait for its QA fixer, re-test in TFactory. One bounded cycle per invocation; it stops when the run passes, when the same tests keep failing (no progress), or when the correction-cycle cap is hit and a human is needed.

skills.name: spec-create
skills.description: Create a test spec for a branch or PR from its acceptance criteria, optionally restricted to specific lanes. Returns a spec id and the RFC-0001 correlation key.

skills.name: spec-run
skills.description: Execute the generated suite for a spec in the sandbox, optionally for a subset of the five lanes.

skills.name: spec-report
skills.description: Fetch the triage report and the 5-signal verdict for a spec: coverage delta, stability, mutation score, lint and semantic relevance, with the ranked findings a human or an agent should act on.

skills.name: handback
skills.description: Route a correction back to AIFactory's QA fixer when the verdict fails: the failing tests plus the report, keyed by correlation key so the fix lands on the original build.

service.name: cfactory
service.title: CFactory
service.description: The control tower. CFactory threads each unit of work across PFactory -> AIFactory -> TFactory using a WorkItem correlation store keyed by the RFC-0001 correlation key, ingesting completion events on a webhook and streaming the cockpit over WebSocket. It is a pure consumer: it observes the other services and only writes through copilot actions, which are prepared first and executed only on human confirmation.

skills.name: workitems-list
skills.description: List work items, optionally filtered by project or status. A work item is one unit of work threaded across the whole fleet, so this is the fastest way for an agent to see everything currently in flight.

skills.name: workitem-get
skills.description: Fetch the aggregated state of one work item across all four services by its RFC-0001 correlation key: where the plan, the build and the verification each stand, in one object.

skills.name: workitem-timeline
skills.description: Get the ordered completion events for one work item - the audit trail of what each service did and when. Use it to answer 'why is this stuck' without opening four portals.

skills.name: usage-aggregate
skills.description: Aggregate token and cost usage by service, project or work item. Metered providers report currency; subscription and local providers report tokens and time.

skills.name: copilot-advise
skills.description: Prepare - but do not execute - an action against a work item, such as a rerun or a handback. Returns a prepared action describing exactly what would happen. This is the only way CFactory writes anything, and it is deliberately a two-step.

skills.name: copilot-confirm
skills.description: Execute a previously prepared copilot action. Requires the action id from copilot-advise and represents the human-in-the-loop confirmation step; nothing mutates without it.
